title: Button help tooltip reopens and sticks after closing the st.dialog it opened
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a button with `help=` opens an `st.dialog`, closing the dialog brings the button's tooltip back. It then stays open until the pointer moves over the button or the user clicks somewhere else. This happens with centered dialogs and with `position="right"` drawers, and with every way of closing (✕, clicking outside, or a button inside the dialog that calls `st.rerun()`).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st


[USER].dialog("Centered dialog")
def centered():
    st.write("Close me with the X, Esc, clicking outside, or the button.")
    if st.button("Close"):
        st.rerun()


[USER].dialog("Right drawer", position="right")
def drawer():
    st.write("Close me with the X, Esc, clicking outside, or the button.")
    if st.button("Close"):
        st.rerun()


st.subheader("With help (bug)")
if st.button("Open dialog", help="This tooltip reappears after the dialog closes."):
    centered()
if st.button("Open drawer", help="This tooltip reappears after the drawer closes."):
    drawer()

st.subheader("Without help (control)")
if st.button("Open dialog (no help)"):
    centered()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and click **Open dialog** with the mouse.
2. Close the dialog with the mouse (✕, click outside, or **Close**).
3. Leave the mouse still, away from the button.

### Expected Behavior

The tooltip stays hidden. Focus going back to the button is correct for accessibility, but focus restored by code (or caused by a mouse click) shouldn't open the tooltip.

### Current Behavior

The tooltip of **Open dialog** is shown as soon as the dialog closes and doesn't go away until the pointer moves over the button or something else is clicked. **Open drawer** behaves the same. The control button has no tooltip, so nothing appears.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.66.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

**Root cause and suggested fix**

In `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/Tooltip/Tooltip.tsx`, `TriggerArea` opens the tooltip for any focus within the trigger:

```tsx
const { focusWithinProps } = useFocusWithin({
  onFocusWithin() {
    hasFocusWithinRef.current = true
    if (!disabled) state?.open(true)
  },
  onBlurWithin() {
    hasFocusWithinRef.current = false
    state?.close(true)
  },
})
```

and `onPointerLeave` skips closing while focus is held:

```tsx
onPointerLeave={() => {
  if (!hasFocusWithinRef.current) {
    state?.close(closeImmediatelyOnPointerLeave)
  }
}}
```

When the dialog closes, focus is restored to the trigger button. `onFocusWithin` opens the tooltip, and because focus stays on the button, moving the pointer away doesn't close it.

Treating only keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`) as "focus held" looks like a small fix, with no new dependency:

```tsx
onFocusWithin(e) {
  // Keyboard focus only: not mouse clicks or focus restored when a dialog closes
  hasFocusWithinRef.current =
    (e.target as Element).matches?.(":focus-visible") ?? true
  if (!disabled && hasFocusWithinRef.current) state?.open(true)
},
```

`onBlurWithin` and `onPointerLeave` can stay as they are. Keyboard users still get the tooltip when they tab to the button, or when they close the dialog with Esc. Mouse users no longer get a stuck tooltip.

Notes:

- `isFocusVisible()` from React Aria would be the natural helper, but it isn't exported from the main `react-aria` entry point yet (adobe/react-spectrum#10666).
- jsdom doesn't model input modality, so the unit tests can't catch this. A Playwright test that opens a dialog from a button with `help`, closes it with the mouse, and asserts the tooltip isn't visible would.

Possibly related: #13263 (focus-visible styling after opening a dialog via a shortcut), and #17489 / #17502 (tooltip rework).

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-17562)

This is a frontend bug: an `st.button` with `help` reopens its tooltip and leaves it on screen after the `st.dialog` it opened is closed. It happens for centered dialogs and `position="right"` drawers, and for every close path in the report (close button, outside click, Escape, or an inner button that calls `st.rerun()`). React Aria’s dialog overlay restores focus to the opener button. `TriggerArea` in `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/Tooltip/Tooltip.tsx` treats any focus inside the trigger as a reason to open immediately (`useFocusWithin` → `state.open(true)`), which skips the 500ms hover delay used for button help. `onPointerLeave` then leaves the tooltip open while that focus remains, so it stays visible with the pointer still elsewhere until the button blurs. That focus-within behavior has been in place since the BaseWeb tooltip replacement (#15310). #17489 and #17502 are the later React Aria / Floating UI tooltip updates; they changed portal placement, and the open-on-any-focus path predates them. Keyboard focus (Tab, and Escape when focus is restored as keyboard focus) should still show the tooltip. jsdom does not model input modality, so a Playwright test is the right coverage.

### Related Issues

- [#13263](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13263) (closed): opening a dialog with a button shortcut left a focus-visible ring on controls inside the dialog. Adjacent dialog focus-modality bug; closed as fixed after the React Aria migration. The stuck tooltip is a separate failure on the opener after close.
- [#9243](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9243): the first widget inside `st.popover` or `st.dialog` appears active when the overlay opens. Also dialog focus, on content inside the overlay.
- [#12649](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12649): `help` on `st.button` never appears on mobile. Same button help tooltip, with touch as the missing trigger.

No open issue describes this same tooltip reopening after a dialog closes.
